items.title: The restaurants
items.text: Most became Hardee’s from 1982, starting with nearly 260 company-owned units. Franchisees could convert, rebrand or close.[^7][^10] Many of the buildings still stand under other uses.[^8][^24]

items.title: The last franchise
items.text: Cookeville, Tennessee, kept the name until 1996, when it became “Pleasers.”[^4] One local history attributes its long survival to a franchisee lawsuit settlement; we could not confirm that account.[^9]

items.title: The trademark
items.text: Hardee’s Food Systems held two Burger Chef registrations, issued in 1993 and 1994. River West Brands petitioned to cancel them as abandoned in January 2007 and withdrew in April 2009.[^13][^14] We have not checked their status since.

items.title: The Big Shef
items.text: Hardee’s sold it for a limited time in 2007 in Indianapolis, Terre Haute, Fort Wayne, South Bend and Dayton, at two for $3, and again in Indianapolis in 2014.[^11][^12] An Indiana history blog also records a 2001 run.[^8]

items.title: The owners
items.text: General Foods moved on to Oscar Mayer.[^2] Hardee’s was later bought by CKE Restaurants, the owner of Carl’s Jr., and was a wholly owned CKE subsidiary by 2007.[^9][^11]

items.title: Speedway
items.text: The 1978 murders of four employees remain unsolved. The Indiana State Police renewed its appeal for information on the 40th anniversary in 2018.[^15][^16]

blocks.title: Who owned the name
blocks.subtitle: Three owners in the chain’s working life, and a fourth by acquisition of the third.

nodes.owner: The Thomas brothers and Robert Wildman
nodes.what: General Equipment’s owners open the first Burger Chef in Indianapolis and franchise it.[^5][^6]
Buys about 700 units and expands to 1,200 outlets. Discloses an $83 million loss in 1972.[^1]
Buys the chain and converts the restaurants to Hardee’s.[^3][^10]
A petition to cancel the trademarks as abandoned is filed and later withdrawn.[^13][^14]

CKE, the owner of Carl’s Jr., buys Hardee’s in 1997 according to one local history.[^9] Hardee’s keeps the trademark and uses it for occasional Big Shef promotions, most recently documented in 2014.[^11][^12]
